newsitem.title: USA: Insituform, holders settle proxy contest.
newsitem.headline: Insituform, holders settle proxy contest.

text.p: A group including two Insituform Technologies Inc directors said Tuesday they and the company on July 3 agreed in principle to settle a proxy contest for the election of slate of nominees to the board.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the group including dissident directors Jerome Kalishman and Robert Affholder said under terms of the agreement, the company's board of directors would be reduced to nine from 13.
They also said the current staggered terms of the directors would be eliminated and there would be no contested election of directors prior to the 1999 annual meeting.

The agreement in principle is subject to the execution of a definitive agreement, the approval of the full board of directors of the company and approval by the stockholders at the 1997 annual meeting schedule for August 21.
Under the terms of the agreement in principle, the company's board of directors would consist of seven current directors and two new independent directors.
The current seven are: Robert Affholder, Paul Biddleman, Anthony Hooper, Jerome Kalishman, Silas Spengler, Sheldon Weining, Russell Wight, Jr.
The new independent director is Stephen Cortinovis and another independent director to be named later, according to the filing.
The proxy contest by the pair to replace three directors was first made public on June 23.
Insituform,, based in Memphis, Tenn., is a sewer, water, gas and industrial pipe repair company.
